extracted.intended_audience: general readers, potential subscribers, advertisers, and newsroom stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: An institutional 'About Us' page describing The Hindu newspaper's history, editorial stance, products, coverage footprint, and subscriber benefits. Useful for understanding the publisher's standards, offerings, and positioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust as primary asset
rubrics_metrics.description: "The greatest asset of The Hindu, founded in September 1878, is trust."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions trust/credibility as the key evaluative quality; implies that reporting and editorial choices should build and maintain reader trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent editorial stand
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial independence is stated as an institutional principle; content and opinion should reflect independence from undue influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliable and balanced presentation of the news
rubrics_metrics.description: "...and its reliable and balanced presentation of the news have over the years, won for it the serious attention and regard of the people who matter in India and abroad."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should be accurate, reliable, and balanced; this is an explicit quality expectation tied to reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong reportage from key locations
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Hindu is known for its strong reportage from the national capital as well as from the southern States and cities."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes depth and strength of on-the-ground reporting from particular geographies (national capital, southern states); a criterion for coverage emphasis and resource allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wide network of correspondents and photographers
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Hindu has a wide network of full-time and part-time correspondents and photographers across India."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining a broad reporting and visual journalism network is presented as necessary for comprehensive coverage and quality reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early and significant digital presence
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Hindu has a major presence online: it was the first Indian newspaper to start an Internet edition, in 1995. The Hindu's digital versions, including the website, app, and e-paper, cater to an ever growing audience."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital reach, multiple digital formats (website, app, e-paper), and innovation/adoption of online editions are treated as important standards for serving audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localized/tailored editions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Tailored in parts to suit different circulation regions for unique news and advertisement content, it has more than 40 different versions produced each day."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producing region-specific editions and tailoring content and ads to circulation regions is a guideline for relevance and local engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensive print production footprint
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Hindu is printed in 19 centres across the country."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A large printing/distribution footprint is presented as part of the publication's capability to reach diverse regions; a logistical/quality criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group publishing diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: The group publishes related titles: "BusinessLine... Frontline... Sportstar."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining specialized sister publications (business, fortnightly in-depth magazine, sports weekly) is part of offering depth across beats and formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial accountability and corrections processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Links and sections such as "Corrections & Clarifications" and "Readers Editor-Terms of Reference" are listed on the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit mechanisms for corrections and a Readers' Editor indicate standards for accountability, error correction, and reader redress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Editorial Values
rubrics_metrics.description: The page links to a "Code of Editorial Values."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An explicit editorial code frames principles and standards journalists and editors are expected to follow; points readers to formalized values and guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth of topical coverage and structured sections
rubrics_metrics.description: The site lists many sections and topics (India, World, Sport, Business, Science, Technology, Health, Life & Style, Books, Elections, etc.) and multiple newsletters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wide topical breadth and organized sections/newsletters are positioned as a standard for comprehensive news coverage and audience segmentation; the presence of newsletters implies editorial curation for topic-specific audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscriber/member benefits and access controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentions: "Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more." Also: "Access 10 free stories every month; Save stories to read later; Access to comment on every story; Sign-up/manage your newsletter subscriptions..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the functional benefits offered to subscribers/members and access restrictions for non-subscribers; relevant for evaluating user experience, engagement features, and paywall policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and customer support availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides customer support contact (customersupport@thehindu.co.in, 1800 102 1878) and 'Contact Us' links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability of support channels is an operational standard for subscriber service, inquiries, and issue resolution.
